items.title: Physicists trap and tame single particle of antimatter for months
items.summary: For the first time, Northwestern University physicists have coaxed a single positron—the antimatter counterpart of an electron—into an exquisitely controlled quantum state.

items.title: How climate change, new technology are shaping the future of extremes in peak power demands
items.summary: New research led by the University of Michigan provides utilities and policymakers with forecasts that can help them better prepare for future extremes in peak energy demand in the United States.

items.title: Bering Sea heat wave linked to a surprising boom in the number of hybrid crabs
items.summary: Marine heat waves are usually seen as destructive events that can disrupt entire ocean ecosystems and trigger massive environmental damage. In 2018 and 2019, an extreme heat wave hit the Bering Sea, causing spring sea ice levels to plummet.

items.title: Kissing bugs can spread potentially fatal Chagas disease when dogs eat them
items.summary: In the southern United States and across Latin America, kissing bugs can bite people and pets both outdoors and when they enter homes. items.title: Bereaved people from ethnically diverse communities are being let down by support services, study finds
items.summary: The England-wide study involving 121 bereaved people from 13 ethnic backgrounds found that racism, language barriers and a lack of culturally appropriate support continue to prevent many people from accessing help after the death of someone close to them.

items.title: Giant Jurassic fossil sheds light on the evolution of a six-legged predator
items.summary: Insects belong to a broader group of six-legged animals called hexapods. This group also includes other less well-known, small animals, including diplurans or two-pronged bristletails, wingless relatives of insects with two rear projections called cerci that resemble feelers or pincers.

items.summary: Bacteria get a bad reputation—with all the outbreaks, infections and deaths.

items.title: Massive study of 460,000 people challenges ultra-processed food cancer fears
items.summary: A massive study of more than 460,000 Americans found that ultra-processed foods were not associated with increased colorectal cancer risk overall, challenging a widely held assumption. items.title: Australia urged to put biodiversity at the heart of planning as global targets slip out of reach
items.summary: The world is falling short of its biodiversity commitments because nature is still treated as an afterthought in decisions about housing, infrastructure, agriculture, energy, mining and conservation, according to a new UNSW report.

items.title: Too much RNA can starve cells of energy, scientists discover
items.summary: Scientists have uncovered an unexpected danger lurking inside cells: too much RNA can damage the structures responsible for producing energy. items.title: Tackling Lake Erie's algal blooms requires targeted conservation strategies
items.summary: Anyone living along the coast of Lake Erie will be well aware of the periodic algal blooms that appear on its surface. The greenish blooms can cause rashes and other health problems and pose risks to both humans and animals.
